page: Amazon Web Services h1.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. System memory totals 128 GB of RAM, offering a 4 GB memory allocation per vCPU core. The hardware configuration includes 45 MB of L3 cache, a bundled local storage capacity of 8,000 GB on magnetic HDD disks, and a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core CPU capacity coupled with lower single-core processing capabilities. Single-core tests such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core score in the bottom 10%, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing showing similar lower-tier performance. Multi-threaded evaluations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU, PassMark CPU score, bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang, fall into the middle 50% average tier. Large block memory write bandwidth scores in the bottom 25%, while Redis SET throughput and static web serving remain in the middle 50% average range.

With 8,000 GB of local HDD storage paired with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance emphasizes dense local capacity over high-speed random write IOPS. The trade-off involves relying on older CPU architecture and magnetic disk storage, which limits single-threaded responsiveness while delivering steady multi-core execution. The h1.8xlarge is best suited for storage-dense workloads, including log processing, distributed data analytics, batch data processing, and large file repositories.
